This anti-inflammatory effect highlights ISOGK's therapeutic potential for atherosclerosis intervention, supported by transcriptomic profiling.

Short Abstract: This research explores the inhibitory mechanism of Banxia Xiexin Decoction on gastric cancer. It identifies differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in AGS and SUN cell samples treated with various concentrations of the decoction, analyzing DEGs between treatment groups and cell lines using multi-omics approaches.
Keywords: Banxia Xiexin Decoction;gastric cancer;inhibitory mechanism;serum pharmacochemistry;network pharmacology;transcriptomics;differentially expressed genes

Project Title: Effect of artemisinin derivatives on the expression of genes related to oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma
Short Abstract: Artemisinin derivative (DHA) inhibits PDGF-BB secretion in oral tongue squamous carcinoma cells, thereby weakening tumor cell reprogramming effects on the tumor microenvironment. This provides new theoretical support for the anti-tumor mechanisms of natural product derivatives.

Project Title: Prim-O-glucosylcimifugin Attenuates TGF-?|??-Induced Fibrosis via MAPK Pathway Inhibition and ECM Remodeling in Intestinal Fibroblasts
Short Abstract: Prim-O-glucosylcimifugin (POG) attenuates TGF-尾-induced intestinal fibrosis in fibroblasts. It inhibits MAPK/Smad signaling and promotes ECM degradation by modulating MMP1/TIMP1. These findings suggest POG as a promising therapeutic candidate for intestinal fibrosis in IBD.

Project Title: RNA sequencing of C elegans exposed to natural polyphenols
Short Abstract: C. elegans worms were exposed to honokiol or magnolol. Global transcriptomic profiles were determined to elucidate the potential modes of action of these natural polyphenols, providing insights into their biological effects.
Keywords: honokiol;magnolol;C. elegans;RNA sequencing;transcriptomics;natural polyphenols

Project Title: Large scale cell-based transcriptome data treated with Jakyakgamcho-tang in PC12 cell
Short Abstract: Whole transcriptomic analysis was performed on PC12 cells treated with different concentrations of Jakyakgamcho-tang extracts (JGT-E and JGT-W). The study compared gene expression profiles between treated and vehicle-controlled cells to understand the formula's effects at a molecular level.
Keywords: Jakyakgamcho-tang; PC12 cells; transcriptome; gene expression; herbal medicine

Project Title: Oridonin as a Novel KDM5C Inhibitor Alleviates Clonal Hematopoiesis Induced Cardiac Aging via H3K4me3 Dependent SASP Suppression [RNA-seq]
Short Abstract: Oridonin, identified via transcriptome screening, alleviates clonal hematopoiesis-induced cardiac aging. It inhibits KDM5C histone demethylase, reversing age-associated myocardial fibrosis, inflammation, and senescence. This mechanism involves downregulating pro-senescent factors and suppressing SASP-associated inflammation, thereby attenuating cardiac remodeling and functional decline.

Project Title: Erianin induces apoptosis and pyroptosis via MAPK/ERK and PI3K/Akt pathways and synergizes with anlotinib in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
Short Abstract: Erianin, a natural compound from Dendrobium, demonstrates significant anti-tumor effects on anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) in vitro and in vivo. It induces apoptosis and GSDME-dependent pyroptosis in ATC cells, potentially via MAPK/ERK and PI3K/Akt pathways, and synergizes with anlotinib.

Project Title: Investigating the molecular mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effects of Detumescence Analgesic Plaster on knee osteoarthritis through RNA sequencing technology
Short Abstract: This study explores the molecular mechanisms of Detumescence Analgesic Plaster (DAP) for knee osteoarthritis (KOA) using RNA sequencing. It identified key genes (e.g., NDUFA5, NDUFA6, NDUFS6, COX6A2) enriched in oxidative phosphorylation, showing DAP's therapeutic effects on cartilage tissue.

Project Title: The effect of LIG (ligustilide) on gene expression in liver of mice undergoing BDL-induced liver fibrosis.

Project Title: Bulk RNA sequencing on hepatic tissues from colitis mice treated with a sublethal indirubin dose.
Short Abstract: This study investigates how indirubin, a poorly soluble indigo naturalis component, induces hepatic injury in chronic colitis mice. Short Abstract: This study used high-throughput sequencing to explore inflammation-related gene expression in LPS-stimulated Raw264.7 macrophages pretreated with Lespedeza bicolor root components, identifying NF-κB and p38 signaling pathways as interesting targets.
Keywords: Lespedeza bicolor root;LPS;Raw264.7;high-throughput sequencing;inflammation;NF-kappaB;p38 signaling pathway

Project Title: Highly-conserved lncRNAs regulates the BRCA1 locus under broad-stress responses [RNA-Seq]
Short Abstract: Novel, highly conserved lncRNAs (TILR-1, TILR-2, LINC00910) are identified, regulating the BRCA1 locus transcription in human cells. This lncRNA network is activated under broad cellular stress responses like triptolide, heat shock, and arsenic.

Project Title: Evaluation of the pharmacological effects of oridonin on hepatic ischemia/reperfusion injury in vivo
Short Abstract: This study evaluates the protective effects of oridonin, a natural diterpenoid compound, against hepatic ischemia/reperfusion injury (IRI) in an in vivo model. Project Title: Gene expression analysis of IL-17 induced mice small intestinal smooth muscle strips with or without 6-shogaol.

Short Abstract: MiRNA sequencing profiles were analyzed in brain and intestinal tissues of mice with ischemic stroke and gut dysbiosis after Xinqingning Tablet treatment to understand its therapeutic mechanisms.

Project Title: Deer Antler ASCs Exosomes Ameliorate Osteoarthritis via miR-140/MMP13 Axis-Mediated Dual Modulation of Inflammation and Cartilage Regeneration

Short Abstract: Bojungikki-tang (BJT) was evaluated for its ameliorative effect on psoriasis-like dermatitis. Project Title: Effect of electroacupuncture on the skeletal muscle atrophy induced by hindlimb suspension in mice

Short Abstract: This study compares gene expression in Artemisia annua seedling and mature leaf tissues, which possess contrasting artemisinin content. Microarray analysis was employed to identify differentially expressed genes associated with artemisinin production in these plant tissues.

Short Abstract: This study profiles *Candida albicans* gene expression, comparing fluconazole treatment with a combination of fluconazole and berberine, and berberine alone, to understand transcriptional responses.

Short Abstract: This study explored Salvianolic Acid B's therapeutic mechanisms in atherosclerosis (AS) via tsncRNAs. SalB significantly increased tRNA-Glu-CTC-014 and tRNA-Gly-GCC-074, identifying them as potential targets whose genes are involved in protein binding, cellular processes, and MAPK signaling.

Short Abstract: Sparstolonin B (SsnB), isolated from *Sparganium stoloniferum*, exhibits anti-angiogenic properties by inhibiting endothelial cell tube formation and migration. Short Abstract: This study analyzes miRNA transcript levels after exposure to triptolide in vitro and its prodrug minnelide in xenograft pancreatic tumor models, exploring their impact on gene expression.

Short Abstract: This study examines genome-wide expression profiles in HepG2 liver cells after treatment with berberine chloride. It aims to reveal the molecular changes induced by this compound, offering insights into its potential therapeutic mechanisms.

Short Abstract: This study investigated gene expression profiles in the substantia nigra of MPTP-intoxicated mouse brains, a parkinsonism model, after acupuncture at acupoints GB34 and LR3. Short Abstract: Antrodia cinnamomea extract globally downregulates miRNAs, including oncogenic miR-21 and miR-191, and alters mRNA transcriptome in hepatocarcinoma cells (SK-HEP-1) within 2-4 hours. Short Abstract: Ginkgolic acids and Ginkgo biloba extract effectively inhibit E. coli O157:H7 biofilm formation without affecting bacterial growth. They represent a non-toxic therapy by repressing curli and prophage genes, suggesting plant secondary metabolites as biofilm inhibitors.

Project Title: The effect of berberine upon HepG2 cell viability
Short Abstract: This study investigates berberine's inhibitory effect on HepG2 cell viability, aiming to determine the genes regulated by berberine and clarify the possible molecular mechanisms underlying its action.

Short Abstract: This study aims to identify microRNA expression profiles induced by wogonin treatment in human head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) cell lines, using miRCURY LNA microRNA Array.

Short Abstract: This study compares frankincense and sandalwood essential oils' cytotoxicity in bladder cancer cells. Short Abstract: This study investigated the impact of berberine, an isoquinoline alkaloid, on microRNA expression profiles in primary human hepatocytes. Short Abstract: This study investigates the microRNA and gene expression profiles in primary human hepatocytes following treatment with berberine chloride, aiming to understand its cellular effects.

Project Title: Genome-wide profiling of gene expression under electro-acupuncture treatment on MI heart in rats
Short Abstract: This study conducted genome-wide RNA-seq to profile gene expression in rat models of myocardial ischemia (MI) treated with electro-acupuncture (EA). Short Abstract: This study employs network pharmacology to elucidate the multi-compound, multi-target, and multi-pathway mechanism of action of the Chinese medicine QSYQ in treating myocardial infarction. Project Title: Next Generation Sequencing facilitates analysis of gene expression from Rehmannia glutinosa associated with  replanting disease
Short Abstract: This study used RNA-seq to analyze gene expression in Rehmannia glutinosa to investigate transcriptional changes associated with replanting disease. Project Title: The effect of Gelsevirine on ischemia penumbra
Short Abstract: Gelsevirine plays an important role in modulating neuroinflammation within the ischemia penumbra. This research investigates its effects on this critical brain region, highlighting its therapeutic potential.

Project Title: Identification of candidate targets for Haizao Yuhu Decoction acting on goiter rats
Short Abstract: This study aimed to identify candidate targets for Haizao Yuhu Decoction in goiter rats by comparing gene expression levels between control, model, and treatment groups, thereby predicting differential genes involved in its action.

Short Abstract: This study investigated miRNA expression profiles in breeder cock testes following dietary Astragalus Polysaccharide (APS) intake. We identified differentially expressed miRNAs between APS-fed and control groups, suggesting APS influences testicular miRNA expression.

It compared treated cells to control cells to identify differentially altered microRNAs, aiming to understand their role in berberine's pharmacological effects and potential toxicity.
Keywords: berberine;microRNA;hepatocytes;expression profiling;pharmacological effects;toxicity

Project Title: Identification of genes involved in the anti-inflammatory effects of berberine in DNP-activated mouse MC/9 mast cells
Short Abstract: This study identifies genes involved in the anti-inflammatory effects of berberine in DNP-activated mouse MC/9 mast cells. Global gene expression analysis elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which berberine mitigates inflammatory responses, offering insights into its potential for treating inflammatory conditions.
Keywords: berberine;anti-inflammatory;gene expression;mast cells;atopic dermatitis

Project Title: Exploring the mode of action of anti-mycobacterial activity of C17 diynes using microarray
Short Abstract: This study explores the anti-mycobacterial mode of action of C17 diynes, falcarinol and panaxydol, via microarray. It suggests these compounds inhibit fatty acid biosynthesis, especially phospholipid synthesis, in mycobacteria, distinct from common drugs.
Keywords: C17 diynes; falcarinol; panaxydol; anti-mycobacterial activity; mode of action; microarray; Mycobacterium smegmatis; fatty acid biosynthesis; phospholipid synthesis

Project Title: The effects of herb-partitioned moxibustion on miRNA expression profiling in the colons of CD rats
Short Abstract: This study investigated the effects of herb-partitioned moxibustion on miRNA expression profiles in the colons of Crohn's disease rats. It identified miR-147 and miR-205 as significantly regulated target genes of herb-partitioned moxibustion, highlighting its therapeutic potential.
Keywords: herb-partitioned moxibustion;miRNA;Crohn's disease;miR-147;miR-205
Institution: Shanghai Medical College of Fudan University

Project Title: Expression of microRNAs in rat kidney treated with a carcinogenic dose of Aristolochic Acid
Short Abstract: This study investigates microRNA expression in rat kidneys treated with a carcinogenic dose of Aristolochic Acid (AA). Rats received 10 mg/kg AA or vehicle control for 12 weeks. Deep sequencing of eight kidney samples (four treated, four control) was performed to profile miRNA regulation in AA-induced carcinogenesis.
Keywords: Aristolochic Acid;microRNA;kidney;carcinogenesis;rat

Project Title: RNA-seq data from MCF-7 cells (breast cancer model) treated with soy extracts
Short Abstract: RNA-seq data from MCF-7 breast cancer cells treated with soy botanical extracts (genistein, S-equol, liquiritigenin) under various ER尾 and ERα expression conditions were analyzed to investigate their effects on gene expression.
Keywords: MCF-7 cells;breast cancer;soy extracts;genistein;S-equol;liquiritigenin;RNA-seq;estrogen receptor

Project Title: Radiation effects on a 3D cell culture of primary human keratinocytes and the protective effect of N-acetyl-cysteine and the Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) Qingre-Liyan decoction
Short Abstract: This study investigated radiation effects on 3D human oral keratinocyte cultures, modeling oral mucositis. It examined the protective effects of N-acetyl-cysteine and Qingre-Liyan decoction against radiation-induced damage, including apoptosis and histological changes.
Keywords: Radiation;oral mucositis;3D cell culture;keratinocytes;Qingre-Liyan decoction;N-acetyl-cysteine;radioprotection

Project Title: Microarray gene expression profiles of peripheral blood mononuclear cells in patients with advanced stage non-small cell lung cancer treated with first line combination chemotherapy with or without Rikkunshito treatment
Short Abstract: This study investigates the effects of Rikkunshito on microarray gene expression profiles in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) of advanced-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients undergoing first-line combination chemotherapy. It aims to link gene expression changes with Rikkunshito treatment during chemotherapy.
Keywords: Rikkunshito;NSCLC;gene expression;microarray;chemotherapy;PBMC

Project Title: Sequencing and de novo analysis of Oviductus Ranae initial growth transcriptome using Illumina RNA-Seq Technology
Short Abstract: This study employed Illumina RNA-Seq technology for sequencing and de novo analysis of the Oviductus Ranae initial growth transcriptome. It aimed to provide an overview of its gene expression profile during this crucial period.
Keywords: Oviductus Ranae;transcriptome;RNA-Seq;de novo analysis;gene expression
Institution: Center for New Medicine Research, Changchun University of Chinese Medicine

Project Title: Differential actions of selective frankincense essential oil versus non-selective sandalwood essential oil induced bladder cancer cell cytotoxicity: A microarray and bioinformatics approach
Short Abstract: This study compares frankincense and sandalwood essential oils' cytotoxicity in bladder cancer cells. Frankincense exhibits selective action and NRF-2 mediated oxidative stress, while sandalwood induces DNA damage and cell cycle arrest, differentiating their anti-neoplastic mechanisms.
Keywords: frankincense;sandalwood;essential oil;bladder cancer;cytotoxicity;microarray;bioinformatics;Boswellia carterii;Santalum album;anti-proliferation;apoptosis

Project Title: Application of a 9k-cDNA microarray for identification of albendazole and artemisinin targeting genes in Echinococcus granulosus larval protoscoleces
Short Abstract: This study utilized a 9k-cDNA microarray to identify gene expression profiles in *Echinococcus granulosus* protoscoleces treated with albendazole and artemisinin. It revealed distinct sets of up-regulated and down-regulated genes, suggesting different molecular targets related to energy metabolism, cell cycle, and genetic information for the two drugs.
Keywords: albendazole;artemisinin;Echinococcus granulosus;cDNA microarray;gene expression;protoscoleces
Institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

Project Title: Triptolide alters the miRNA expression profiles in human hepatocellular carcinoma HepG2 cells
Short Abstract: This study investigated the effects of triptolide on miRNA expression profiles in human hepatocellular carcinoma HepG2 cells. miRNA expression was compared among HepG2 cells treated with various concentrations of triptolide (0, 100, 200 nM) for 12 or 24 hours.
Keywords: triptolide;miRNA expression;HepG2 cells;hepatocellular carcinoma

Project Title: Genome-wide dynamics of Pol II elongation and its interplay with promoter proximal pausing, chromatin, and exons
Short Abstract: The study investigates genome-wide Pol II elongation dynamics in mouse ES cells using Triptolide and Flavopiridol inhibitors. It reveals that pause escape is a crucial, ubiquitous step, Pol II is stable, and elongation rates vary, accelerating through genes but slowing at exons, influenced by chromatin and genomic features.
Keywords: Pol II elongation; promoter proximal pausing; chromatin; exons; GRO-seq; mouse ES cells; Triptolide; Flavopiridol; gene transcription; H3K79me2

Project Title: Global transcriptome analysis of fungal genes affected by a novel antifungal agent KR-72, a 13-(4-isopropylbenzyl)berberine derivative   a 13-(4-isopropylbenzyl)berberine derivative
Short Abstract: KR-72, a novel berberine derivative, shows enhanced antifungal activity against pathogenic fungi. Transcriptome analysis in Cryptococcus neoformans reveals KR-72 alters gene expression, upregulating translation/transcription genes and downregulating metabolism. It also promotes essential gene expression, providing insights into its antifungal mechanism.
Keywords: KR-72;berberine derivative;antifungal activity;transcriptome analysis;Cryptococcus neoformans;mode of action

Project Title: The effect of Sparstolonin B (SsnB) on gene expression in HCAECs
Short Abstract: Sparstolonin B (SsnB), a novel bioactive compound from the TCM herb Sparganium stoloniferum, inhibits endothelial cell tube formation and migration. This study used microarrays to examine SsnB's effect on gene expression in human coronary artery endothelial cells (HCAECs), focusing on angiogenesis-related pathways.
Keywords: Sparstolonin B; SsnB; Sparganium stoloniferum; gene expression; HCAECs; angiogenesis; microarray

Project Title: The effect of Sparstolonin B (SsnB) on gene expression in HUVECs
Short Abstract: Sparstolonin B (SsnB), a novel compound from Sparganium stoloniferum, exhibits anti-angiogenic properties by inhibiting endothelial cell tube formation and migration. This study investigated SsnB's effect on gene expression in HUVECs via microarrays, focusing on angiogenesis-related pathways after 24 hours of exposure.
Keywords: Sparstolonin B;SsnB;gene expression;HUVECs;angiogenesis;Sparganium stoloniferum;microarray

Project Title: microRNA expression profile of wogonin treatment in HNSCC cell lines
Short Abstract: This study aimed to identify microRNAs induced by wogonin treatment in human head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) cell lines. FaDu and SAS cell lines were treated with wogonin, and differentially expressed microRNAs were analyzed using a microRNA Array.
Keywords: wogonin;microRNA;HNSCC;cell lines;expression profile
Disease: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

Project Title: Plant Leaves: Pinellia pedatisecta vs Pinellia ternata
Short Abstract: This study profiles miRNA expression in Pinellia pedatisecta leaves, comparing them to Pinellia ternata leaves. It identifies differential miRNA accumulation between these two independently grown Pinellia species using microarray signals under the same conditions.
Keywords: Pinellia pedatisecta; Pinellia ternata; miRNA expression profiling; microarray; differential expression; plant leaves

Project Title: Expression profile of LNCaP prostate cancer cell line treated with DMSO or BP
Short Abstract: This study investigates N-butylidenephthalide (BP)'s antitumor effects and mechanisms in LNCaP prostate cancer cells. It aims to identify gene expression alterations induced by BP treatment using microarray analysis to understand BP-induced cell death.
Keywords: N-butylidenephthalide;BP;prostate cancer;LNCaP;gene expression;antitumor;microarray

Project Title: Comparison of root transcriptomes and expression of genes involved in main medicinal secondary metabolites from Bupleurum chinense and B. scorzonerifolium, the two Chinese official Radix bupleuri source species
Short Abstract: This study compares root transcriptomes and gene expression involved in main medicinal secondary metabolites from two Radix bupleuri source species, Bupleurum chinense and B. scorzonerifolium, using 454-FLX pyrosequencing and qRT-PCR. Findings reveal differences in metabolic pathways and gene expression related to terpenoid, triterpenoid, sterol, lignan, and flavonoid biosynthesis, providing insights for their rational application.
Keywords: Radix bupleuri;Bupleurum chinense;Bupleurum scorzonerifolium;transcriptome;secondary metabolites;gene expression;saikosaponins
Institution: Institute of Medicinal Plant Development (IMPLAD), Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

Project Title: The genes affected by Triptolide in activated  mouse primary T cells
Short Abstract: This study investigates triptolide's immunosuppressive mechanism on mouse primary T cell activation and proliferation. Using microarrays, global gene expression changes and effects on TCR/AP-1 pathways were detailed, providing insights into its action.
Keywords: Triptolide; immunosuppression; T cells; gene expression; microarray

Project Title: Anti-Stress Effect of Red Ginseng via Repression of PADI4 by ER-beta Stimulation
Short Abstract: This study investigates the anti-stress effects of red ginseng by analyzing its impact on gene expressions in immobilization-stressed mice brains. It suggests a mechanism involving ER-beta stimulation and PADI4 repression, analyzed via system biology.
Keywords: Red Ginseng;anti-stress;gene expression;immobilization stress;PADI4;ER-beta stimulation;system biology
Institution: Ajou univ, Suwon, Republic of korea

Project Title: Identification of genes responsive to change in apical polarity in the breast epithelium
Short Abstract: This study identifies genes responsive to apical polarity changes in breast epithelial acinar cells using 3D culture and microarray analysis. It investigates how polarity loss affects cell quiescence and tissue homeostasis by comparing polarized and non-polarized cells.
Keywords: apical polarity;breast epithelium;gene identification;microarray analysis;3D cell culture;cell quiescence;tissue homeostasis

Project Title: Transcriptome and microRNA array analyses reveal a stimulatory effect of the phytochemical shikonin on epithelial?¨Cmesenchymal transition (EMT) in mouse skin
Short Abstract: Transcriptome and microRNA array analyses demonstrated that the phytochemical shikonin has a stimulatory effect on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in mouse skin. This research utilized gene expression and microRNA expression profiling to explore its molecular mechanisms.
Keywords: shikonin;epithelial-mesenchymal transition;EMT;transcriptome;microRNA;mouse skin

Project Title: Transcriptome and microRNA array analyses reveal a stimulatory effect of the phytochemical shikonin on epithelial?¨Cmesenchymal transition (EMT) in mouse skin [microRNA expression profile]
Short Abstract: This study investigates shikonin's in vivo effects on mouse skin, revealing its stimulatory role in epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) through transcriptome and microRNA array analyses. Shikonin upregulates EMT regulatory molecules and downregulates specific microRNAs like miR-200 family and miR-205, confirming its potent effect on skin EMT.
Keywords: shikonin;epithelial-mesenchymal transition;EMT;microRNA;transcriptome;mouse skin

Project Title: Expression data from Xenopus laevis liver
Short Abstract: Xenopus CAR is identified as a novel xenobiotic receptor, responsive to drugs like artemisinin. This study uses artemisinin and pregnenolone treatments in Xenopus laevis livers to identify xlCAR target genes via microarray analysis.
Keywords: Xenopus laevis;CAR;PXR;xenobiotics;artemisinin;pregnenolone;microarray;liver

Project Title: Transcriptomics of the traditional Japanese medicine juzentaihoto (JTX) on germfree mice
Short Abstract: This study investigates the transcriptomic effects of the traditional Japanese medicine Juzentaihoto (JTX) on both large and small intestines in germ-free mice. It explores gene expression changes induced by JTX in a controlled microbial environment across two distinct intestinal regions.
Keywords: Transcriptomics; Juzentaihoto; JTX; germfree mice; large intestine; small intestine; traditional Japanese medicine

Project Title: Gene expression data from liver of rat fed a high-fat diet and high-fructose water without/with Eucommia ulmoides leaves
Short Abstract: This study investigated the effects of Eucommia ulmoides leaves on hyperlipidemia in rats fed a high-fat diet. Gene expression profiling in rat liver showed that Eucommia ulmoides leaves up-regulated genes involved in fatty acid oxidation, mainly via the PPAR signaling pathway.
Keywords: Eucommia ulmoides leaves; hyperlipidemia; gene expression; fatty acid oxidation; PPAR signaling pathway
Institution: Tokyo University of Marine Science and Technology

Project Title: Modulation of growth and angiogenesis of OSCC cells with Sal B
Short Abstract: This in vitro study investigated the inhibitory properties and underlying mechanisms of Sal B on the growth and angiogenesis of OSCC cells. Two OSCC cell lines were treated with Sal B, and cDNA microarray was used to evaluate the expression of angiogenesis-related genes.

Institution: Ninth People's Hospital, School of Stomatology

Project Title: Gene expression data from cervical spinal cord regions of MPTP-intoxicated mouse by acupuncture
Short Abstract: This study investigated gene expression changes in the cervical spinal cord of MPTP-intoxicated mice following acupuncture at GB34 and LR3. The research aims to elucidate the neuroprotective mechanisms of acupuncture in a Parkinson's disease model by analyzing spinal cord gene profiles.
Keywords: acupuncture;gene expression;MPTP;Parkinson's disease;cervical spinal cord;acupoints GB34;acupoints LR3
Institution: East-West Medical Research Institute, Kyung Hee University

Project Title: Role of MicroRNA-214 in Ginsenoside-Rg1-induced Angiogenesis
Short Abstract: Ginsenoside-Rg1, an active component of ginseng, induces angiogenesis by down-regulating microRNA-214, which subsequently increases endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) expression in human umbilical vein endothelial cells. This reveals a novel mechanism for Rg1's angiogenic effects.
Keywords: Ginsenoside-Rg1; angiogenesis; miR-214; eNOS; HUVEC; microRNA

Project Title: Global transcriptional profiling of Saccharomyces cerevisiae treated with dictamnine
Short Abstract: This study investigated the global transcriptional profiling of Saccharomyces cerevisiae treated with dictamnine. The methodology involved yeast incubation with dictamnine, RNA extraction, microarray hybridization, scanning, and data analysis to identify changes in gene expression profiles.
Keywords: dictamnine;Saccharomyces cerevisiae;transcriptional profiling;microarray
Institution: College of Animal Science and Veterinary Medicine, Jilin University

Project Title: Whole genome analysis in A549 cells treated for short incubation periods with various concentrations of triptolide
Short Abstract: This study identified genes primarily affected by short-term treatment of A549 cells with varying concentrations of triptolide. Whole human genome microarray experiments were performed on RNA extracted from cells exposed to triptolide for 1, 2, and 4 hours.
Keywords: triptolide;A549 cells;whole genome analysis;gene expression;microarray

Project Title: Transcript Profiling of Spinal Dorsal Horn in Response to Electroacupuncture on Rats at 24h
Short Abstract: This study investigates transcript profiles in the spinal dorsal horn of rats 24 hours after electroacupuncture (EA). It aims to uncover molecular mechanisms underlying individual variability (high vs. low responders) in EA-induced analgesic effects, using cDNA microarrays to compare gene expression changes.
Keywords: Electroacupuncture;analgesic effect;spinal dorsal horn;transcript profiling;individual variability;rats

Project Title: Global transcriptional profiling of Staphylococcus aureus treated with magnolol
Short Abstract: This study investigates the global transcriptional profiling of Staphylococcus aureus treated with magnolol, a compound with potent antimicrobial activity. Given the rise of multi-resistant S. aureus strains, magnolol represents a potential new agent, and gene expression arrays reveal its effects.
Keywords: Staphylococcus aureus; magnolol; transcriptional profiling; antimicrobial activity; gene expression array
Institution: College of Animal Science and Veterinary Medicine, Jilin University

Project Title: Global transcriptional profiling of Staphylococcus aureus treated with sodium houttuyfonate
Short Abstract: This study investigates the global transcriptional profiling of Staphylococcus aureus treated with sodium houttuyfonate. Sodium houttuyfonate, a potent antimicrobial agent, was used to treat drug-resistant S. aureus, revealing insights into its mechanism of action.
Keywords: sodium houttuyfonate;Staphylococcus aureus;transcriptional profiling;antimicrobial activity;gene expression array
Institution: College of Animal Science and Veterinary Medicine, Jilin University

Project Title: Analysis of Gene Expression in Ginger Tissues at Different Developmental Stages
Short Abstract: This study analyzed gene expression in rhizome, root, and leaf tissues of Yellow ginger at various developmental stages (2-7 months). An interwoven loop design was used for hybridizations to compare different stages and tissues grown under controlled greenhouse conditions.
Keywords: Ginger; gene expression; developmental stages; rhizome; root; leaf; microarray; Yellow ginger

Project Title: Transcript Profiling of Spinal Dorsal Horn in Response to Electroacupuncture on Rats at two time points
Short Abstract: This study investigates transcript profiling in the spinal dorsal horn of rats in response to electroacupuncture stimulation. Transcriptomic changes were analyzed at two distinct time points (1 hour and 24 hours) to understand temporal molecular responses.

Project Title: Transcript Profiling of Spinal Dorsal Horn in Response to Electroacupuncture on Rats at 1h
Short Abstract: This study profiles spinal dorsal horn transcripts in high and low responders to 2Hz/100Hz electroacupuncture in rats, exploring individual variability in analgesia. It identified co-regulated plasticity genes and distinct neurotransmitter/cytokine and ribosome-related gene differences between responders.
Keywords: Electroacupuncture; Transcriptome profiling; Spinal dorsal horn; Individual variability; Analgesia; Gene expression; Rats; High responders; Low responders; cDNA microarray; Plasticity

Project Title: Transcription profiling of rat sarcopenic skeletal muscle after treatment with extract of Ginko biloba Egb 761 shows that a juvenile gene expression profile is reactivated
Short Abstract: This study investigates Ginkgo biloba extract (EGb 761) effects on sarcopenic skeletal muscle in aged rats. EGb 761 reactivated a juvenile gene expression profile related to regeneration and energy production, improving muscular performances. It modulates myogenesis and reverses age-related metabolic shifts, suggesting a novel treatment for sarcopenia.
Keywords: Ginkgo biloba extract;EGb 761;sarcopenia;skeletal muscle;transcription profiling;gene expression;myogenesis;energy metabolism

Project Title: Reciprocal regulation of genes expression by Ephedra herba in mouse brain
Short Abstract: Aqueous extracts of Ephedra herba, administered orally to mice, reciprocally altered gene expression in brain tissue. Microarray analysis revealed dose and time-dependent changes in gene expression, classifying into two major reciprocal patterns.
Keywords: Ephedra herba;gene expression;mouse brain;microarray analysis;reciprocal regulation

Project Title: Transcription profiling of human androgen starved LNCaP cells treated with celastrol and androgen, androgen alone, or vehicle alone for 24h
Short Abstract: This study investigated the transcriptional profiling of human androgen-starved LNCaP cells treated with celastrol. Researchers used microarrays to detail the androgen-responsive gene expression program affected by 24-hour treatment with celastrol plus androgen, androgen alone, or vehicle alone, providing insights into celastrol's impact on androgen signaling.
Keywords: celastrol;LNCaP cells;androgen signaling;gene expression;transcription profiling;microarray
Institution: Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT

Project Title: Transcription profiling of rat skeletal muscle after fine needle stimulation
Short Abstract: This study examined gene expression in rat skeletal muscle following fine needle stimulation (acupuncture). Building on previous findings of enhanced neovascularization and blood perfusion in ischemic muscle, microarray analysis was performed 24 hours post-stimulation to evaluate its molecular effects.
Keywords: fine needle stimulation;acupuncture;skeletal muscle;gene expression;microarray;rat;hindlimb ischemia

Project Title: RNA-seq of Rattus novergicus brain after stroke with Yangyin Tongnao granules for the treatment of the cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury
Short Abstract: This study investigates the molecular mechanism of Yangyin Tongnao granules against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats using RNA-seq transcriptomics. It aims to identify how the granules reverse stroke-induced differentially expressed targets, providing insights into their therapeutic effects.
Keywords: Yangyin Tongnao granules;cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury;ischemic stroke;RNA-seq;transcriptomics;Rattus novergicus

Project Title: Microarray analysis of MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells treated or not with phytoestrogen Emodin
Short Abstract: This study investigated the gene expression profiles of estrogen receptor-positive MCF-7 and estrogen receptor-negative MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells treated with phytoestrogen Emodin. Microarray analysis revealed gene expression changes in response to Emodin treatment.
Keywords: Emodin;phytoestrogen;breast cancer;MCF-7;MDA-MB-231;microarray analysis;gene expression

Project Title: RNA-seq of mouse primary somatosensory cortex (S1) in a neuropathic pain model after electroacupuncture stimulus
Short Abstract: This study investigates the molecular mechanisms in the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) that underlie the pain-relief effects of electroacupuncture in a neuropathic pain model, utilizing RNA-seq analysis.
Keywords: electroacupuncture;neuropathic pain;RNA-seq;somatosensory cortex;molecular mechanism

Project Title: The differentially expressed genes of  Zucker Diabetic Fatty Rats treated with Berberine against diabetes mellitus
Short Abstract: This study investigates the anti-diabetic effects of Berberine (BBR), a key alkaloid from Rhizoma Coptidis, by elucidating its genome-wide gene expression profile in the liver tissues of Zucker Diabetic Fatty rats, addressing its mechanism of action against diabetes.
Keywords: Berberine;diabetes mellitus;differentially expressed genes;Zucker Diabetic Fatty Rats;gene expression profile;Rhizoma Coptidis

Project Title: Effects of Morus alba L. (Mulberry) Leaf Extract in Hypercholesterolemic Mice on Suppression of Cholesterol Synthesis
Short Abstract: This study investigated the effects of Morus alba L. (mulberry) leaf extract on hypercholesterolemia. Microarray analysis revealed that the extract up-regulated genes suppressing cholesterol synthesis and stimulating innate-adaptive immunity, suggesting its potential in managing high cholesterol.
Keywords: Morus alba L.; Mulberry leaf extract; Hypercholesterolemia; Cholesterol synthesis; Gene expression
Institution: Tokyo University of Marine Science and Technology

Project Title: Expression data from Colossolactone H treated H1650 cells
Short Abstract: Colossolactone H, isolated from Ganoderma colossum, was investigated for its anticancer mechanism in human lung cancer H1650 cells. Microarray analysis revealed gene expression changes, providing insights into its molecular mechanism.
Keywords: Colossolactone H;Ganoderma colossum;lung cancer;H1650 cells;gene expression;microarray

Project Title: Jinfukang induces cellular apoptosis through activation of Fas and DR4 in A549 cells
Short Abstract: Jinfukang (JFK), a traditional Chinese medicine, demonstrates efficacy against non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study investigates JFK ethanol extract's antitumor mechanisms by showing it induces cellular apoptosis through Fas and DR4 activation in A549 lung cancer cells, analyzed via RNA-seq assays.

Project Title: Microarray to identify the differentially expressed genes in CFG treated SKOV3 cells compared with control cells under TGFbeta condition
Short Abstract: This study used microarray analysis to identify differentially expressed genes in ovarian cancer cells (SKOV3) treated with Compound Fuling Granule (CFG) under TGF-beta conditions. The analysis revealed potential regulation of cell cycle and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) related genes by CFG, providing insights into its anti-cancer mechanism.

Project Title: The effect of XUESAITONG on gene expression profile after focal cerebral ischemia in rats
Short Abstract: This study investigates the effect of Xuesaitong injection, a Chinese patent medicine derived from Panax notoginseng, on gene expression profiles after focal cerebral ischemia in rats. Using whole genome microarray analysis, researchers aim to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of XST's therapeutic effects against ischemic stroke.
Keywords: Xuesaitong;gene expression;focal cerebral ischemia;rats;Panax notoginseng;ischemic stroke;microarray

EA at acupoints PC3 and PC6 improved colitis symptoms by downregulating cytokine gene expression and affecting inflammatory and immunity pathways, as revealed by transcriptomic analysis.

Project Title: Transcript profiles of the flowering period Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer root and analysis the gene function
Short Abstract: Transcript profiles of flowering period Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer root were analyzed using Illumina sequencing to identify genes related to flowering, antifungal proteins, and transcription factors for stress. Project Title: Genome-wide analysis of berberine chloride-responsive gene expression in HepG2 liver cell line
Short Abstract: This study analyzed genome-wide gene expression profiles in HepG2 human hepatoma cells after berberine chloride treatment using microarray. It aimed to identify berberine-responsive genes, providing insights into its pharmacological effects on liver cells.

Short Abstract: Celastrol, a natural product from Thunder God Vine, targets PRDX1 to inhibit colorectal cancer cell proliferation. A derivative, 19-048, also demonstrated efficacy. Project Title: De Novo Transcriptome Sequencing in Oviductus Ranae of Rana chensinensis Using Illumina RNA-Seq Technology
Short Abstract: De novo transcriptome sequencing was performed on Oviductus Ranae from Rana chensinensis using Illumina RNA-Seq. The study aimed to profile gene expression during hibernation, offering insights into its molecular mechanisms and biological processes.

Project Title: Transcription of muscle actin genes by a nuclear form of mitochondrial RNA polymerase
Short Abstract: This SuperSeries provides gene expression data from MCF-7 and HUVSMC cells, investigating transcription. Experiments include treatment with PolII inhibitors like Triptolide and knockdown of POLRMT or RNA PolII.

Project Title: Gene expression data from brain striatal and spinal cord regions of MPTP-intoxicated mouse following acupuncture
Short Abstract: This study investigates gene expression changes in brain striatal and spinal cord regions of MPTP-intoxicated mice following acupuncture intervention. It comprises two subset series focusing on distinct brain areas to understand acupuncture's therapeutic mechanisms at the molecular level.
Keywords: Acupuncture;gene expression;MPTP;striatal;spinal cord;mouse model

Project Title: Gene expression data by the leaves of Eriobotrya japonica (Ej) on the LPS-stimulated human gingival fibroblast
Short Abstract: This study investigated gene expression changes in LPS-stimulated human gingival fibroblasts treated with Eriobotrya japonica (Ej) leaves. Using microarray, researchers analyzed RNA from control, LPS-treated, and LPS-Ej co-treated fibroblast groups to understand Ej's effects on inflammation.

It activates protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) in podocytes, which decreases inflammation and high glucose-induced migration, establishing PP2A as a therapeutic target for DKD.
Keywords: Arctigenin;diabetic kidney disease;DKD;PP2A;podocytes;renoprotection;Fructus Arctii
Institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

Project Title: Illumina sequencing reveals conserved and novel microRNAs involved in dendrobine biosynthesis in Dendrobium nobile
Short Abstract: Illumina sequencing identified conserved and novel miRNAs in Dendrobium nobile protocorms and leaves. These miRNAs are involved in metabolic pathways and regulate enzymes crucial for dendrobine biosynthesis and plant hormone signal transduction, offering insights for yield enhancement.
Keywords: Dendrobium nobile;dendrobine;microRNAs;Illumina sequencing;terpenoid biosynthesis;plant hormone;protocorm

Project Title: Regulation effect and mechanism of Sheng-Hua-Tang on female reproductive system: from experimental transcriptomic analysis to clinical applications
Short Abstract: Sheng-Hua-Tang (SHT) is a traditional formula commonly used for postpartum conditioning. This study investigates its effects and mechanisms on the female brain-ovary-uterus axis, combining experimental transcriptomic analysis with clinical applications to elucidate its regulatory role in the female reproductive system.
Keywords: Sheng-Hua-Tang;female reproductive system;transcriptomic analysis;postpartum conditioning;brain-ovary-uterus axis;clinical applications

Project Title: miRNA expression profiling in cervical cancer cells following emodin treatment
Short Abstract: This study aims to investigate the role of emodin in cervical cancer by profiling miRNA expression changes. Emodin has shown potential in inducing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Analyzing differentially expressed miRNAs will clarify how emodin regulates cervical cancer pathogenesis and treatment.
Keywords: emodin;miRNA;cervical cancer;expression profiling

Project Title: Development of gene expression signatures using herbal drug ninjin'yoeito (NYT)
Short Abstract: This study aimed to identify hematopoietic genes regulated by Ninjin'yoeito (NYT). Microarray analysis was performed to compare bone marrow mononuclear cells cultured with and without NYT for 11 days, revealing specific gene expression signatures.
Keywords: Ninjin'yoeito; NYT; gene expression signatures; hematopoietic genes; microarray analysis; herbal drug

Project Title: Potentiating the activity of berberine for Staphylococcus aureus in a combinatorial treatment with thymol
Short Abstract: This study used RNA sequencing to explore the combinatorial effect of berberine, an antibacterial alkaloid, and thymol, a monoterpenic phenol, on Staphylococcus aureus transcriptome, aiming to potentiate berberine's activity.
Keywords: berberine;thymol;Staphylococcus aureus;combinatorial treatment;RNA sequencing;transcriptional profiling;antibacterial

Project Title: Unique microRNA Alterations in Hepatocellular Carcinomas Arising Either Spontaneously or due to Chronic Exposure to Ginkgo biloba Extract (GBE) in B6C3F1/N Mice
Short Abstract: This study investigated unique microRNA alterations in hepatocellular carcinomas induced by Ginkgo biloba extract (GBE) in mice. It identified differentially altered miRNAs and suggested some could serve as potential biomarkers for GBE exposure or carcinogenesis, enhancing understanding of GBE-mediated hepatocarcinogenesis.
Keywords: Ginkgo biloba extract; hepatocellular carcinoma; microRNA; hepatocarcinogenesis; biomarker

Project Title: Integrative analysis of lncRNAs, miRNAs, and mRNA-associated ceRNA network in lung tissue of aging mice and changes after intervention of Codonopsis pilosula
Short Abstract: This study performs an integrative analysis of lncRNAs, miRNAs, and mRNA-associated ceRNA networks in the lung tissue of aging mice. It also investigates the alterations in this network following intervention with Codonopsis pilosula.

Project Title: Expression data from eight patients with coronary heart disease before and after Tongmai Yangxin Pills treatment for eight weeks.
Short Abstract: This study investigated genomic changes in eight coronary heart disease patients treated with Tongmai Yangxin Pills for eight weeks. Microarrays were used to explore the underlying mechanisms of this patented medicine, known for its anti-inflammatory effects in CHD treatment.

Project Title: RNA-seq in liver cancer cell and cinobufagin treatment cells
Short Abstract: Cinobufagin, derived from toad venom, exhibits significant anticancer properties by inhibiting Na+/K+-ATPase. This study investigates its mechanism in liver cancer cells using RNA-seq, revealing that cinobufagin triggers protective autophagy via the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway, and combining it with autophagy inhibitors may enhance its efficacy.

Short Abstract: Galangin, a natural flavonoid, suppresses H19 expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells, promoting apoptosis and inhibiting tumor growth in vivo. Its mechanism involves regulating H19/miR675 and p53, suggesting galangin's therapeutic potential for HCC by modulating H19 expression.
Keywords: galangin;H19;hepatocellular carcinoma;apoptosis;miR675;p53

Project Title: miRNA profiling of Hepa1-6-bearing mouse model
Short Abstract: This study utilized a Hepa1-6-bearing mouse model to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of Ganoderma lucidum extract (GLE) against tumor growth. GLE effectively inhibited tumor growth and modulated miRNA profiles, identifying 25 differentially expressed miRNAs, including 24 up-expressed and one down-expressed miRNA.

Project Title: Bruceantin targets HSP90 to overcome resistance to hormone therapy in castration-resistant prostate cancer
Short Abstract: Bruceantin, a potent HSP90 inhibitor, targets androgen receptor activity and downregulates target genes in castration-resistant prostate cancer cells. This suggests its potential to overcome resistance to hormone therapy.

Project Title: RNA-seq analysis of  active anthraquinones as anti-biofilm agents of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
Short Abstract: This study employed RNA-seq analysis to elucidate the anti-biofilm mechanisms of active anthraquinones, specifically 2-Carboxyanthraquinone and Rhein, against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).

Short Abstract: This study investigated the effects of Paeonia lactiflora extract on cisplatin-induced muscle wasting and its molecular mechanism, specifically focusing on the downregulation of muscle-specific E3 ubiquitin ligases.

Short Abstract: This study identified a synergistic compound combination from Chinese herbal medicine for rheumatoid arthritis therapy. Short Abstract: A candidate beta-glucosidase gene in Platycodon grandiflorus converting platycoside E to platycodin D was identified by correlating metabolite content and gene expression between callus and leaf, advancing understanding of saponin biosynthesis.

Short Abstract: This study investigates the effects of Korean Red Ginseng (KRG) on Di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)-induced inflammatory responses in endometrial cancer Ishikawa cells. Short Abstract: This study analyzes the genome-wide expression profile of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) treated with Ganoderma lingzhi oligopeptide. Short Abstract: This study identified putative genes involved in alkaloid biosynthesis in Dendrobium officinale. Short Abstract: This study used RNAseq analysis to investigate the antibacterial mechanism of Cinnamomum camphora essential oil against Escherichia coli. Short Abstract: This study uses mRNA-seq and miRNA-seq to identify molecular mechanisms, important factors, and target genes regulating fruiting body induction in Ophiocordyceps sinensis. Project Title: Genetic and pharmacological evidence for kinetic competition between alternative poly(A) sites in yeast - 4tU cordycepin treatment
Short Abstract: This study investigates the genetic and pharmacological effects of cordycepin and 4-thiouracil (4tU) on alternative poly(A) sites and 3'UTR length in yeast. It utilizes an mPAT approach with 4tU labeling to analyze changes in transcription and 3'UTR processing.

Short Abstract: Next-generation sequencing analyzed epidermal transcriptomes in imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like dermatitis treated by Xiao-Yin-Fang (XYF). Short Abstract: This study investigated Angelica Gigas Nakai (AGN) extract and its pyranocoumarins (D/DA) in TRAMP mice.
